entriesCount: {total} registration entry/entries, of at most {max} (spiffe.maxEntries). The store is the embedded directory under {container}: an ldapmodify there, a form here and the SPIRE Server API's BatchUpdateEntry are three doors onto one entry, and nothing caches it — so a change takes effect on the next SVID.
entriesSearchPlaceholder: a SPIFFE ID, a selector, an entry id
originNote: Origin is how the entry got here: seed at startup, console, api, grpc, auto (invented for a workload that matched nothing) or ldap.
postureNotAttested: Nothing here is attested. A real SPIFFE agent reads the peer credentials of its socket — pid, uid, gid, and from those the executable, the container, the pod — and hands a workload only the identities those selectors match. Node cannot read them at all, so this service identifies a Workload API caller by the transport it arrived on, the endpoint it reached and its peer address, and nothing else. Those DO now decide which entries answer (spiffe.attestWorkloads), and they prove nothing about who is calling: anybody who can reach the socket can still get an identity. Node attestation is not: an agent below attested with a type its realm accepts and an attestor here verified, or it was refused.
postureServerApiMtls: The SPIRE Server API is the exception. Its TCP port is mutual TLS: a caller presents an X509-SVID from this trust domain, and every method is authorized against SPIRE's own table — so an entry marked admin or downstream below now decides what its holder may do. Its Unix socket is the local entity and needs no credential. The Workload API is deliberately untouched: its specification says a client MUST NOT be required to authenticate.
postureServerApiOpen: And nobody is authenticated on the SPIRE Server API either. That port is plain gRPC, any caller can create a registration entry granting any identity here and then collect an SVID for it, and the admin and downstream flags below are recorded and read by nothing. It is restart-only, because it decides how the socket is bound.
postureSeeSpiffe: {link} has the whole table and the full list of what is and is not checked.
createEntryNote: The SPIFFE ID must be in this trust domain and outside the reserved /spire path — those two refusals are the whole of what is checked. The parent defaults to this server's own identity, which is what SPIRE uses for an entry describing a workload rather than a node.
selectorsSyntaxNote: Selectors, DNS names and trust domains are comma-separated. A selector is type:value, split on the FIRST colon only — so docker:label:app:web is type docker.
noAgents: No agent has attested here. An agent appears when it calls AttestAgent on the SPIRE Server API.
agentsCount: {total} agent(s), of at most {max} (spiffe.maxAgents). These entries are a RECORD rather than configuration — everything on them was written by this service when an agent attested — which is why nothing about an agent is editable and only the ban is.
nodeAttestationNote: Node attestation is verified or refused. An agent here attested with a type its realm names in spiffe.nodeAttestors and an attestor verified, and its selectors are the ones that attestor derived.
agentsSearchPlaceholder: an agent id, an attestor, a selector
noBrokers: No broker is authorized, so every call to the SPIFFE Broker API is refused PERMISSION_DENIED.
brokersNotListening: not listening in this realm: spiffe.brokerPort is {port}
brokersIntro: The SPIFFE Broker API (Incubating) lets a trusted infrastructure component ask for the SVIDs of a workload it REFERENCES — a process id, or a Kubernetes pod — which this service attests itself before answering. It is served with mutual TLS on spiffe.grpcHost and spiffe.brokerPort ({where}). A caller presents an X509-SVID, and one whose SPIFFE ID is not listed here is refused.
brokersPidNote: A process id means something only on the node it was read on. The endpoint is TCP, so allow pid only to a broker running on this host; k8s resolves a pod in this node's kubelet pod list.
brokersSearchPlaceholder: a SPIFFE ID or a reference type
brokerSaveNote: A broker already listed has its reference types replaced. An ID from a federated trust domain is verified against that domain's bundle.
entryNotFound: No registration entry has the id {id}. It may have been deleted — from this page, with BatchDeleteEntry, or with an ldapdelete under ou=entries,ou=spiffe, which are three doors onto one store.
entryLives: Entry {id}, revision {revision}, created by {origin}. It lives at {dn}.
entryLivesExpired: Entry {id}, revision {revision}, created by {origin}. It lives at {dn} and has expired — it is kept and reported rather than deleted, because an entry that vanished is indistinguishable from one nobody created.
flagsNeverRead: recorded and never read — nothing here decides anything on one
changeItNote: Only the DECLARED half is editable here — what the entry may DO. The derived half (the revision number, the SVID counter, when it was created) is what HAPPENED, and a form that could rewrite it would make this page lie about the service's own behaviour. ldapmodify reaches everything: refusing it here is the difference between offering an operation and merely not preventing it.
setFieldNote: A list field takes comma-separated values and an empty value clears it. A boolean takes true or false.
deleteEntryNote: Whatever holds an SVID minted from it keeps that SVID until it expires. SPIFFE has no revocation — the answer is a short lifetime, which is why the default is an hour.
directoryEntryNote: Every attribute, operational ones included. This is the store rather than a description of it.
agentNotFound: No agent has attested here as {id}.
agentHeader: Attested with {type}, {count} time(s), first at {first} and most recently at {last}. It lives at {dn} — the RDN is a digest of the SPIFFE ID, because a SPIFFE ID is too long for a readable one, so the cn is not the identity here: spiffeAgentId is.
bannedExplained: banned — AttestAgent refuses it, which is one of the few refusals in this service and is what keeps the button below from being a lie
itsDirectoryEntryText: Every identity this trust domain issues an X509-SVID to has one under ou=users, carrying the current certificate as the same six x509* attributes a verified TLS client certificate writes. Banning or deleting this agent marks that entry spiffeCredentialStatus: revoked and never removes it; unbanning marks it active again.
notACertStatus: That is not a certificate status. SPIFFE has no revocation, nothing reads the flag back, and whatever SVID this agent holds keeps working until it expires.
banNote: A banned agent is refused at AttestAgent with PermissionDenied. Whatever SVID it already holds keeps working until it expires — there is no revocation in SPIFFE.
deleteAgentNote: It reappears the next time it attests, because attestation is not checked — deleting is forgetting, not revoking.
noFederation: None. This trust domain federates with nobody.
pkiManageLink: manage it on the PKI page
spiffeOff: SPIFFE is turned OFF (spiffe.enabled): the bundle endpoint answers 404 and every gRPC call is refused with Unavailable. Turn it back on in the settings at the foot of this page; it needs no restart.
authorityGenerating: The issuing authority is still being generated — an RSA-4096 key takes a few seconds. Reload.
trustDomainNote: This service is the issuing authority for {trustDomainId}. Its own identity as a SPIFFE server is {serverId}, and every registration entry hangs beneath that by default. The trust domain is restart-only (spiffe.trustDomain): every authority certificate names it.
bundleNote: The bundle is published at {link} — sequence {sequence}, refresh hint {hint} seconds. The sequence changes whenever the bundle does and never otherwise, which is what lets a consumer tell “I have the current bundle” from “I have a bundle”.
authorityPki: The X.509 authority is this realm's SPIFFE Issuing CA, under this service's own Root — {pkiLink}, where it is one of the Issuing CAs in this realm's branch. So the trust anchor a consumer installs is the Root, which every realm shares and which also covers LDAPS 636, the main port and every token this service signs: one anchor, installed once. An X509-SVID carries the Issuing CA and this realm's Intermediate in its own chain{chain}. Rotating it re-issues that Issuing CA and leaves the anchor alone, so the bundle does not change, nothing has to be re-fetched, and SVIDs minted under the old authority go on verifying — which is the whole difference from the self-signed arrangement this replaced. The JWT authority has no certificate and no hierarchy to hang from: it is generated per start and rotating it still prepends, keeping at most {maxRetained}.
authoritySelfSigned: This realm has no certificate authority, so its X.509 authority is self-signed and IS the trust anchor — generated per start and held in memory, exactly like the STS signing key and the TLS certificate, so a workload holding a bundle from before a restart will fail to verify every SVID minted after it. Rotating PREPENDS a new authority and keeps the old one published: an SVID minted a minute ago has to go on verifying, which is what a bundle is for. At most {maxRetained} are retained, and past that the oldest is dropped — anything it signed stops verifying at that moment. {buildLink} to put the SPIFFE authority under this service's Root instead.
subject: Subject
rotateNote: New SVIDs are signed with the new authority immediately; existing ones keep verifying until they expire.
grpcListenersNote: Neither /admin/sts-metadata nor this page can see a socket, so this table is the only place that reports whether each one actually bound. The DEFAULT realm's four are bound when the process starts and stay bound with spiffe.enabled off — they answer Unavailable, because a socket that vanished would read as a service that had stopped. EVERY OTHER REALM'S are bound when spiffe.enabled is turned on for it, on the address spiffe.grpcHost names for that realm — the endpoint address is the only thing a SPIFFE client has to name a tenant with, because the gRPC method name is fixed by the specification.
whoMayCall: Who may call the SPIRE Server API
anyOfNote: A caller may be several of these at once and the check asks whether it is any of the ones a method allows, which is what SPIRE's own policy does: the spire-server CLI on this host is local, and an agent that also holds an entry marked admin is both.
adminIdsList: Administrators by configuration (spiffe.adminIds, in the settings at the foot of this page): {ids}.
adminIdsNone: Administrators by configuration (spiffe.adminIds, in the settings at the foot of this page): none.
adminIdsOtherWay: The other way to make one is to mark a registration entry admin on {entriesLink}; SPIRE has both, and neither is cached, so either takes effect on the next call.
workloadSelectorsDecide: Workload API selectors: a caller there is identified as transport:, endpoint:, peer: over TCP, and on the Unix socket by what the workload attestors established (above), and those decide which entries answer it (spiffe.attestWorkloads).
workloadSelectorsDecideNothing: Workload API selectors: a caller there is identified as transport:, endpoint:, peer: over TCP, and on the Unix socket by what the workload attestors established (above), and that decides nothing at the moment — spiffe.attestWorkloads is off, so every caller is answered with every entry.
assertedBelieved: Asserted selectors ({header}) are believed, and nothing verifies them.
assertedIgnored: Asserted selectors ({header}) are ignored (spiffe.acceptAssertedSelectors is off, or this realm is in product mode, where it is never in force).
bothSwitchesInForce: Both switches are what is IN FORCE: in product mode spiffe.attestWorkloads is always on and asserted selectors are never believed, whatever is stored, and neither can be changed to the looser value there.
perMethodNote: Copied from SPIRE's own policy_data.json rather than reasoned out: a table derived from what each method “obviously” needs disagrees with SPIRE in two or three places, and the client author who meets the disagreement cannot tell which end is wrong. any means the method is open here and in a real server too — AttestAgent because an agent has no SVID until that call gives it one, GetBundle because a trust bundle is public.
federatedNote: A foreign bundle is given to this service and never fetched by it. The federation specification has a bundle endpoint URL in the relationship and a real implementation polls it; this one records the URL and refuses to follow it, because fetching a URL somebody registered in order to obtain a credential-verification key is a server-side request forgery with a citation attached — the same refusal this service gives WS-Federation's wreqptr and a client's jwks_uri. Paste the bundle in below, or push it with BatchSetFederatedBundle.
jwkSetNote: A JWK Set. Every key needs use of x509-svid, jwt-svid or wit-svid: a consumer MUST IGNORE one without it, so a bundle of keys missing that member verifies nothing and reports no error, which is why it is refused here rather than stored.
brokerApiBrokersWhat: who may ask for a referenced workload's SVIDs
whatThisIs: What this is, and what it does not check
nothingBound: Nothing bound for {what}. Either both transports are off in configuration, or the process has not finished starting.
nativeLoaded: The native module is loaded: each connection to the Workload API's Unix socket is attested when it is accepted, and every call on it checks that the process is still the one attested.
nativeMissingUnattested: The native module is not loaded, so the Unix socket is served UNATTESTED (development): {problem}
nativeMissingNotServed: The native module is not loaded, so the Unix socket is NOT SERVED (product): {problem}
tcpPort: The Workload API TCP port is {state}{where}: {why}.
attestorsWhich: A TCP caller is never attested. Which attestors run is spiffe.workloadAttestors{unknown}.
attestorsUnknown: ; it names {names}, which nothing here implements
noConnection: No connection is open on the socket now.
